findings.title: UnsupportedOperationException in getKeyFactory and getSignature breaks JWT client credentials
findings.body: `AuthzClient` supports `client-jwt` credentials via `JWTClientCredentialsProvider`, which loads the client's private key from a keystore and signs a JWT using `KeyWrapper` and `AsymmetricSignatureSignerContext`. During that flow, `KeyWrapper` and `KeyUtils` invoke `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getKeyFactory(...)`, `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(...)`, `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getPemUtils()`, and `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getEcdsaCryptoProvider()` (which are also used when verifying tokens or parsing keys). In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getKeyFactory` and `getSignature` throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. When `AuthzClient` runs with `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` as the active `CryptoProvider` (i.e. without `keycloak-crypto-default` on the classpath, which is the scenario this provider is added for), any client authentication or token operation that uses `getKeyFactory` or `getSignature` will fail at runtime with `UnsupportedOperationException`.

findings.title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 sequence or element causes negative allocation or infinite loop
findings.body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when it encounters the indefinite-length byte `0x80` (lines 133-135). However, callers do not handle `-1`: in `readInteger()` and `readNext()`, `read(length)` is called with a negative value (or `length` after `reset()`), throwing `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of `IOException`; in `readSequence()`, `length` is `-1` so the `while (length > 0)` loop is skipped and an empty sequence is returned. In DER encoding, indefinite lengths are invalid and should throw an `IOException` rather than returning `-1`.

findings.title: Redundant unused ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the returned encoders, immediately repeating the exact same work on lines 119-120 inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements allocate `ByteArrayOutputStream`s and encode the integers for no effect.

findings.title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key pair for ES384 and ES512 and does not verify the re-encoded DER signature
findings.body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default `EC` key pair (256-bit) in the constructor and reuses it for `ES256`, `ES384`, and `ES512`, and only asserts that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` -> `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` -> `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` round-trips to the same byte array. It never passes `asn1Des` back to `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` to confirm the DER output produced by `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` is actually valid ASN.1 DER accepted by the JCA `Signature` verifier, nor does it test with 384-bit (`secp384r1`) or 521-bit (`secp521r1`) keys where `r` and `s` have lengths > 127 bytes (which exercises multi-byte ASN.1 length encoding in `ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder`).
